## Natural history notes

A small carpenter bee characterized by its slender, mostly dark metallic body, sparse pale hairs, and habit of carrying pollen on the hind legs. In Florida, it is found in gardens, fields, forest edges, roadsides, pine flatwoods, parks, and other sunny habitats with flowering plants and suitable nesting stems. Adults visit flowers for nectar and pollen, while females nest inside hollow or pithy plant stems, where they create small brood cells for their developing young.
